container: Urbanization changes society by concentrating people, jobs, and services in cities. It can create employment, improve access to education and healthcare, and encourage cultural exchange. Public transport and shared infrastructure may reduce travel costs and support innovation. However, rapid growth can produce overcrowded housing, traffic, pollution, and pressure on water and energy supplies. Rising property prices may push poorer residents into distant neighborhoods, widening social divisions. Urban expansion can reduce farmland and habitats. When cities plan affordable homes, green spaces, and reliable services, urbanization can promote opportunity while protecting health, community ties, and the environment.
